title: perf-bench-scratch-lina-chen-2026-03-04
content:
Scratchpad: latency/throughput runs - rw-7b-q4 / KV cache + batching

Context / goal:
- Quick quant perf sanity checks for rw-7b-q4 (internal shorthand) on prod-like infra (4xA100 pool).
- Measure p50/p95 latency and aggregate throughput for common request mixes: short-chat (32 tokens), medium (128 tokens), long (512 tokens).
- Check impact of prefix KV-cache and continuous batching on latency and tokens/sec.
- Narrow down configs to recommend for hosted default runbook and a gating perf regression test.

Test harness / commands used:
- bench harness: infra/bench/runner.py --model rw-7b-q4 --pool a100-4 --concurrency N --batching-config <cfg> --seq-len L --duration 120s
- simple curl test for single-request latency: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' --header 'Authorization: Bearer ...'
- workload: 50/30/20 split short/medium/long simulated by runner (randomized prompts).

Notes on config knobs tried:
- batching: off / fixed-batch-size (1/4/8) / dynamic (latency-target 120ms)
- kv-cache: disabled / enabled (prefix cache on identical prompt prefixes)
- quant: q4_k_m baseline, q5 trial (not final)
- kernel path: cuda-fused-attn vs baseline-attn (default auto-select)

Raw summarized results (p50/p95 latency in ms, throughput tokens/s aggregated across test):

Table legend: C = concurrency (simulated clients), B = batch size or dynamic, seq = target generated tokens per request.

Results (abridged):
- Test A: C=1, B=1, kv=off
  - seq32: p50=28ms, p95=42ms, tokens/s=850
  - seq128: p50=95ms, p95=150ms, tokens/s=520
  - seq512: p50=360ms, p95=610ms, tokens/s=260

- Test B: C=8, B=dynamic (latency target 120ms), kv=off
  - seq32: p50=65ms, p95=240ms, tokens/s=2800 (aggregate)
  - seq128: p50=140ms, p95=420ms, tokens/s=2100
  - seq512: p50=520ms, p95=1200ms, tokens/s=1500

- Test C: C=8, B=dynamic, kv=enabled (prefix cache hit ~35%)
  - seq32: p50=45ms, p95=160ms, tokens/s=3300 (cache helps short requests)
  - seq128: p50=110ms, p95=330ms, tokens/s=2550
  - seq512: p50=480ms, p95=1050ms, tokens/s=1700

- Test D: C=16, B=fixed-4, kv=enabled
  - seq32: p50=78ms, p95=320ms, tokens/s=6100 (aggregate)
  - seq128: p50=180ms, p95=640ms, tokens/s=4200
  - seq512: p50=640ms, p95=1400ms, tokens/s=2900

Observations / quick interpretation:
- KV cache gives clear latency and throughput improvements for short/medium sequences when cache hit rate >~25%. Short requests benefit the most (prefix reuse common for chat system prompts).
- Dynamic batching increases throughput but can inflate p95 significantly under bursty concurrency; set conservative latency target (100-150ms) for customer-facing SLOs.
- Fixed batch-size (4) produced steady throughput at higher concurrencies but higher p50 for single-request cases compared to dynamic + kv. Good for background/rate-limited workloads.
- For long seq (512) the model compute dominates; batching has diminishing returns for latency (but boosts throughput tokens/s). Cores/SM occupancy must be instrumented further (nvprof/nvtx traces).

Immediate action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Re-run the long-seq (512) experiments with kernel tuning flag --use-fused-attn to verify lower p95 (see PR #812).
- [ ] Add GPU perf counters capture (nvidia-smi dmon + Nsight sampling) for top 3 long runs to understand memory bound vs compute bound behavior.
- [ ] Increase KV-cache synthetic hit to 60% in runner to simulate chat scenarios and measure tail latency improvements.
- [ ] Draft runbook recommendation for hosted default: dynamic batching (latency target 120ms), kv-cache enabled, fixed_fallback_batch=4. Put proposal in Linear RD-1289.
- [ ] Add stable regression test in perf CI that checks p95 short-chat < 200ms on 4xA100 baseline (quant q4_k_m).

Open questions / caveats:
- These tests run on 4xA100 pool; Dedicated customer infra (8xA100 or H100) will have different scaling curves. Need at least one cross-hardware comparison later.
- Model variant naming: rw-7b-q4 is a shorthand; confirm exact artifact/tag used by model onboarding before shipping runbook.
- Network hop (test harness -> endpoint) adds ~5-10ms — most runs were on same-VPC runner but not co-located on same host. For tight SLOs we should run co-located microbench.

Log snippets / commands run:
- runner command used for Test C:
  python infra/bench/runner.py --model rw-7b-q4 --pool a100-4 --concurrency 8 --batching dynamic --latency-target 120 --kv-cache on --seq-dist 50,30,20 --duration 120

- example curl single-request (measured with time):
  time curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"Summarize: ...","max_tokens":32}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer x'
  real 0m0.045 -> ~45ms single-request (matches p50 for cached short case)

Notes-to-self on next iteration:
- Instrument run to log per-request cache-hit flag; currently only aggregate hit reported. Need per-request csv.
- Try q5 quant with nvlink-enabled nodes to see if 10-12% perf boost (tradeoff quality).
- Coordinate with SRE to run a 24h soak with mixed traffic to measure degradation and mem fragmentation.

References:
- Linear ticket RD-1289: experiment plan + resourcing
- PR #812 on runtime: fused-attn kernel opt (pending merge)
- Confluence page: kv-cache + dynamic batching notes (working doc)

Conclusion (quick): kv-cache + dynamic batching (latency-target ~120ms) gives best tradeoff for short/medium interactive workloads; fixed small batches better for throughput-heavy background jobs. Need more traces for long-seq bottleneck analysis and follow-up runs on H100/Dedicated pools before finalizing recommendation.

End of scratchpad.
